name: Hanwha
h1: A new structure deserves connected execution
lede: Hanwha has split its holding company, appointed new leaders at five affiliates and is pushing deeper into US defence shipbuilding. Airtable gives each team one shared place to plan, track and hand over the work.
why_h2: A group being reshaped in real time
why_p: Three moves from the last seven months, each creating cross-affiliate work that rarely fits in one system.

signals.title: Shareholders approve the Hanwha Corp spin-off
signals.body: Shareholders voted 99.95 per cent in favour of splitting Hanwha Corp, moving tech and lifestyle units into a new holding company while defence, shipbuilding, energy and finance stay with the surviving entity.
signals.angle: Separation programmes run on hundreds of handovers. One tracker for owners, dependencies and sign-offs keeps both entities moving.

signals.title: New CEOs at five affiliates
signals.body: Hanwha appointed professional managers as CEOs of Hanwha Aerospace, Hanwha Systems, Hanwha Asset Management, Hanwha Impact and Hanwha Semitech, and promoted Kim Dong-kwan to senior vice chairman.
signals.angle: New leaders need fast visibility of in-flight programmes. Airtable turns scattered status updates into one live view.

signals.title: Hanwha Ocean partners on US naval ship design
signals.body: Hanwha Ocean signed with a US naval ship design firm to accelerate its entry into the American market, building on the group's Philly Shipyard base.
signals.angle: Cross-border programmes with partners and regulators need shared milestones, document status and approvals in one place.

final_h2: Twenty minutes on the post-split agenda
